final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor narrowed and clarified the theory using the same record. That clarification is useful and proportionate: it defeats any clean `compliant` reading and correctly distinguishes aggregate readiness and monitoring posture from satisfaction of the policy predicate for caveat-free certification. But it does not reach `compliant_with_caveats` under the stated criteria, because that outcome requires the policy-compliant caveat or approved risk acceptance to be actually in place, not merely described as the right path. The admissible evidence still shows an open material weakness, an incomplete draft runbook, and a draft model card with unsupported 'no known material limitations' language. So the record supports only a plausible caveated path, not a completed compliant one.
remaining_concerns: The grant-compliance weakness in allowable-cost explanation remains unresolved on the admissible record.
The draft mitigation runbook is still incomplete because owner and alert threshold are TBD, so it does not meet the approved-mitigation predicate in policy.
The current model-card draft says there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with the unresolved issue and the disclosure requirement if it persists at launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the required caveated disclosure has actually been implemented in a final launch artifact.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance before launch.
